title: San Diego County releases annual report highlighting community-focused initiatives - San Diego City Wire
text:
The County of San Diego has released its Annual Report for 2024-25, focusing on collaboration with the community and other local agencies. The report outlines efforts aimed at building a just, sustainable, and resilient future.
This year’s report, titled “Opportunities for All; Strength for Tomorrow,” details progress in several key areas: behavioral health, environmental sustainability, equity, healthy and safe communities, homelessness and affordable housing, as well as public safety and justice reform.
According to the County, the Annual Report summarizes activities during the fiscal year from July 1 to June 30. It also sets out priorities and objectives for the coming year. The County operates with an $8.63 billion budget and provides a range of services that impact nearly every resident.
In unincorporated regions, the County serves as the main government body responsible for services such as law enforcement, fire protection, roads, libraries, and parks. Additionally, it oversees programs that serve all county residents—including social services assistance, health programs, food inspections, elections administration, and foster care.
The report highlights various initiatives. For example, a new program answered 131 calls in its first year; by August 2025 it had responded to over 24,000 calls. Other featured efforts include events organized by probation youth such as a Turkey Trot run and support programs for foster youth leading to educational success.
For more information or to access updates directly from the County News Center via email subscriptions or inquiries can be made through communications@sdcounty.ca.gov or by calling 619-595-4633.
